normal_signature: Rectangular hardboard packaging with a glossy, reflective surface finish
Prominent brand logo or name printed in the upper or central region
Mandatory health warning text occupying the lower third of the front face
Intact, sealed cellophane wrapping covering the entire box
Sharp, well-defined edges and corners with no structural deformation
hypothesized_anomaly_modes: Structural crushing or denting of the box corners or sides due to impact
Tearing or puncturing of the outer cellophane seal exposing the inner cardboard
Severe surface abrasion or scuffing that obscures the printed brand logo or health warnings
Peeling or flaking of the printed label layer from the cardboard substrate
Classify as anomaly if the cigarette pack flap is torn, frayed, or physically damaged, regardless of face orientation.
Flag as anomaly if the pack face features a large diagonal stripe or landscape graphic instead of the standard solid background with leaf logo.
Classify cigarette packs with open top flaps or exposed inner packaging as anomalies.

if the box maintains a rigid rectangular shape with a continuous, glossy surface then lean normal

normal_signature: Single upright plastic beverage bottle centered in the frame
Opaque or translucent cylindrical body with a printed paper or plastic label
Screw-top cap (white, green, or blue) securely fastened at the top
Bottle resting on a white surface against a perforated pegboard background
Label features legible text and graphics without significant distortion
Do not flag label rotation or slight misalignment as an anomaly if the bottle is not perfectly front-facing.
hypothesized_anomaly_modes: Crushed or dented bottle body indicating physical damage or mishandling
Missing, loose, or misaligned cap suggesting a seal failure or manufacturing defect
Torn, peeling, or missing label exposing the plastic underneath
Severe leakage or spillage causing the bottle to sit in a puddle or appear wet
Foreign object or debris attached to the exterior of the bottle
If a drink bottle lacks a visible label or branding on its main body, classify it as an anomaly.

if the cap is missing, detached, or visibly loose then lean anomaly
if the label is torn, peeling, or completely missing then lean anomaly
if the bottle is lying on its side or tilted at an extreme angle then lean anomaly
if the bottle is upright with an intact cap and a fully adhered label then lean normal
if the background is a perforated pegboard and the bottle is centered then lean normal

Lid is sealed with a plastic film or foil layer
Container sits upright on a flat surface
Background features a white pegboard with a grid of holes
Do not flag minor foil lid tears or crinkles as anomalies if they are consistent with standard packaging variations seen in reference images.
hypothesized_anomaly_modes: Structural deformation: The container body is crushed, dented, or bent, compromising its cylindrical shape.
Seal failure: The plastic film or foil lid is torn, punctured, or missing, exposing the contents.
Label damage: The printed surface is significantly scratched, peeled, or obscured, making branding unreadable.
Foreign object contamination: Presence of non-package items (e.g., dirt, other food) on the surface or lid.
Treat any small, irregular white mark or scuff on the printed label surface as a defect, even if the mark is tiny.

if the container is upright and the background is a pegboard then lean normal
